answer: Postal-address anchoring ties each agent to one deliverable mailbox. First, the operator registers an address and the network mails a sealed one-time code. Second, the agent activates only after that code is entered within 14 days, and the address hash joins a duplicate-checked registry. Third, a yearly re-mail audit suspends any identity whose letter bounces. Forging 10,000 fakes needs 10,000 real addresses at $30 each, $300,000 plus a 60-day delivery cycle. Like bees guarding one hive's nectar, each address admits one worker, and at dawn the umber envelopes sort real keepers from fakes.
